stories.title: Pladis Appoints Frankgerald Stepp as Chief Supply Chain Officer
summary: Global snacking company Pladis has appointed Frankgerald Stepp as its chief supply chain officer. Stepp, a former executive at Kerry Group, will officially assume the role in January 2027. He succeeds Mario Reis, who is scheduled to retire at the end of December 2026 after nearly ten years with the business. In his new capacity, Stepp will oversee Pladis' operations spanning across more than 110 international markets.

The leadership change follows significant capital investments by Pladis aimed at strengthening production capacity, improving operational efficiency, and building supply chain resilience. In 2025, the company—whose portfolio includes brands such as McVitie’s, Ülker, and Godiva—invested more than £100 million in capital expenditure. This funding supported network reliability, including a £68 million investment in UK bakeries, facility expansions in Cairo, and operational enhancements in France, Türkiye, and the United States.

Stepp brings extensive industry experience to Pladis, having recently served as chief operations officer of Kerry Group's biotechnology business and global vice-president of manufacturing. His previous background includes leadership positions at ARYZTA, Kraft Foods, and Mondelez International. Pladis Chief Human Resources Officer Geraldine Fraser credited outgoing officer Reis with establishing a strong operational foundation and highlighted Stepp's baking industry expertise as critical for supporting the company's future growth strategy.

stories.title: pladis Launches Second Global Accelerator Programme Targeting Sustainable Nutrition and Ingredient Innovation
summary: Global snacking group pladis, the company behind brands including McVitie’s and Godiva, has launched its second global accelerator programme to collaborate with innovative food-tech start-ups. The initiative focuses on improving product nutrition and developing sustainable solutions in response to rising GLP-1 medication adoption and climate-related supply chain disruptions. Up to 12 selected start-ups will receive technical and operational guidance from pladis experts, with three to six candidates potentially progressing to pilot or co-development phases.

Participation in the programme is free, with applications open until January 15 and operations commencing in March. Pladis is targeting key innovation areas, including fermentation, enzymatic processing, sensory science, natural alternatives to additives, gut health, and functional ingredients. The initiative also seeks to solve challenges surrounding ingredient supply resilience, particularly regarding cocoa crops impacted by adverse weather conditions and disease.

The launch follows an initial accelerator scheme that engaged 12 start-ups supported by 37 mentors across pladis and Yıldız Holding. Technologies highlighted from the prior cohort included Zya's enzyme designed to convert sugar into fiber post-consumption, Fermtech's fermentation method converting food-industry by-products into a cocoa alternative, and Nuritas's use of artificial intelligence to identify bioactive plant peptides for functional food ingredients.
